data.reason: The root page lists all twenty-one commands under the goal each serves, the commands a newcomer runs first, and what a logical path and a record are, which STANDARDS.md 24 requires on one page. It also lists the global flags -C and --personal, which choose the board a run uses, and one line naming at most six of the plugins the board enables, which run as `board <plugin> <capability>`.
costs: Each read of the page can cost 1550 bytes more than the default, about 388 tokens.

data.reason: get has two output formats and --fetch, and a reader needs to know on one page that without --fetch get prints an attachment record and never reaches the store.
costs: Each read of the page can cost 200 bytes more than the default, about 50 tokens.

data.reason: put has seven options of its own (--new, --var, --expect, --batch, --bulk, --file and --wait), and a reader needs to know on one page that with a store --file may write an attachment record in place of the bytes. Its page also ends with the Effects: line and a global flags line that names --no-input.
costs: Each read of the page can cost 420 bytes more than the default, about 105 tokens.

data.reason: refs has five options and two output formats, and a reader needs the from/to line format and the --field encoding on one page to parse its text output. Its page also ends with the Effects: line and a global flags line that names --no-input.
costs: Each read of the page can cost 800 bytes more than the default, about 200 tokens.

data.reason: decide says on one page what the owner's approval, refusal and silence each do, its Effects: line says that it adds, and its global flags line names --no-input, which a program adds to every run.
costs: Each read of the page can cost 60 bytes more than the default, about 15 tokens.

data.reason: Board's tests read its text from a pipe
costs: A picker never asks for a missing argument and `Run::confirm` never asks, even at a terminal, so a person must type every argument and `--yes` as a script does.
Progress never prints, help prints without clap's colours at a terminal, and a table's cells print without their styles.
A text table never fits the terminal's width, so the terminal wraps each line of a table that is wider than the terminal.
